task.title: Replace the Workflows library page with the new system UI design
task.objective: Apply the attached SpecterStudio system UI language to the Workflows library page only, preserving every existing workflow action, permission gate, validation rule, and persistence call.

architecture: Change the Workflows library renderer only; preserve the app shell, route, preload API, workflow profile schema, and main-process persistence.
Reuse the existing Hologram tokens, shared table components, dialogs, and page-chrome action system.
Do not copy demo values or simulated behavior from the attached design artifact.
accessibility: Keep semantic table markup, aria-sort state, accessible names on every control, visible focus styles, keyboard-operable actions, responsive overflow, and reduced-motion behavior.
offline: Do not add remote assets, fonts, scripts, dependencies, or runtime network access.

acceptance.description: The Workflows library uses the attached system design language: page-header primary and secondary actions, a titled table surface with a record count, selectable rows with a bulk-action bar, identity-led main cells, badge status cells, and token-driven numeric and monospace cells, without changing other routes or the app-shell grid.

Every existing Workflows control, permission gate, confirmation dialog, import-conflict flow, filter, sort, and pagination path remains wired to its existing handler and preload channel, and the new bulk actions report partial failure truthfully.
The task records accurate AI-memory and roadmap evidence before terminal closeout.

completion.notes: Owner authorized the push directly. Independent QC APPROVED on its third pass, after two REJECTED passes whose findings are recorded in the qc-review evidence. Status stays 'implemented', not 'complete': the two GUI verifiers that navigate to the Workflows route (verify:e2e-sweep, verify:flow-library) are BLOCKED by the documented host-state electron.launch harness issue, so the redesigned page still has no live GUI assertion. QC's recorded position is that this gap does not block a development push but DOES block a release claim. The bulk-delete partial-failure path is the part of this change least covered by any gate available on this host — it is state sequencing that no static check, build, or token sweep can observe, and it is the single most valuable thing to exercise when the harness is next available.
